text:
alex: quick contract check for /v1/rerank — proposing a small, opt-in change to make tie-breaking deterministic across languages. idea: add optional "tie_policy" enum + explicit "score_scale" semantics. any objections? :eyes:

maria: quick Q — is this a request or response change? we must avoid breaking hosted clients.

alex: request-level optional params only. defaults identical to today so older clients/servers unaffected. sketch:

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "...",
  "candidates": [ {"id":"a","text":"..."}, ... ],
  "tie_policy": "stable" | "shuffle" | "score_then_id",
  "score_scale": "raw" | "normalized" | "softmax"  // default raw
}
```

response shape stays as an array of candidate objects. we'll add optional fields to each item: "score" (float) and "rank" (int). when "score_scale"=="normalized" server guarantees scores in [0,1].

jamal: how exactly are the policies defined? we need deterministic tie rules that survive model/serving changes.

leah: suggestion: "stable" = sort by score desc, then by candidate.id lexicographically, then by original index as final fallback. "shuffle" = pseudo-random shuffle seeded deterministically. "score_then_id" = score desc then id only (no index fallback).

alex: also call out score semantics: higher == better. include examples in the spec.

maria: compatibility note: servers MUST ignore unknown params. adding optional response fields is safe. :+1:

jamal: normalization details? if the model returns logits, are we doing softmax by default? that's expensive for huge candidate lists.

alex: default remains "raw" to avoid perf changes. define two normalized modes: 
- "normalized": min-max across returned candidates -> [0,1] (cheap). if all equal, return 0.5 for each.
- "softmax": compute softmax across candidates (exp/sum) — computationally heavier.
Include exact formulas and numeric-stability notes.

leah: for "shuffle" we need deterministic seeding: prefer request_id if supplied; otherwise derive seed from hash(query + candidate ids + floor(timestamp/60)). document this clearly so different servers produce same order when fed same request id.

maria: SDK follow-up: python/js sdks should expose tie_policy and score_scale args and map enums. tagging @devex to coordinate.

alex: example response to lock fields:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
[
  {"id":"b","score":0.92,"rank":1,"text":"..."},
  {"id":"a","score":0.91,"rank":2,"text":"..."}
]

jamal: streaming clients: behavior unchanged. these fields are appended to final payload; no streaming semantics change.

alex: action items: (1) write API spec PR with enums + formulas (alex) (2) SDK stubs + migration note (maria + devex) (3) unit tests for tie-break combos & score_scale edge cases (jamal) (4) migration docs and rollout notes for customers (leah).

maria: I'll open SDK + migration PRs tomorrow.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for spec draft branch api/rerank-tie-2026 at 1768123800 :rocket:

alex: thanks — ping me on the PR for quick review. :thumbsup:

leah: cc @maria @jamal — please attach tests to rerank e2e job.

jamal: will do. one last nit: prefer parameter name "tie_break" vs "tie_policy"? shorter.

alex: leaning "tie_policy" for clarity in docs. not a blocker.

maria: prototype with "tie_policy"; can rename before GA if UX prefers.

alex: last lock: add clear line in spec: "Service MUST NOT change default ordering semantics for unchanged requests." ensures safe rollouts. :lock:

leah: locking this thread. reply within 24h for objections or I'll mark accepted.

jamal: no objections.

maria: fine from me.

alex: fine.

leah: accepted. closing in 24h. :white_check_mark:
